problem: The figure labels the fuel-air cycle item as 'Variable cp' and the air-standard item as 'Constant cp'. The rest of the chapter defines c_v and the table says 'constant c_v', so the figure names the wrong specific heat for an Otto cycle, where the constant-volume value c_v governs. A student memorising the figure will attach the wrong property to the cycle.
fix: Change the labels to 'Variable c_v' and 'Constant c_v' (or 'variable specific heat c_v') so the figure matches the text and the table.

problem: The section says the fuel-air cycle 'keeps the same cycle shape' and then also says combustion is finite and the pressure rise is not instantaneous. Finite heat release is not constant-volume heat addition, so the cycle shape is not exactly the same as the air-standard Otto; the two statements pull against each other.
fix: Say 'keeps the same cycle outline (compression, heat release, expansion, heat rejection) but the heat release is not instantaneous, so the peak pressure is lower and the cycle is closer to a limited-pressure cycle'.
